draft.title: Diffraction gratings
card: A diffraction grating is a plate with a very large number of narrow, evenly spaced slits. Light passing through all the slits interferes to give bright lines.
Bright lines form at angles where light from neighbouring slits arrives in phase. This happens when d sin θ = mλ, where d is the slit spacing and m = 0, 1, 2 and so on.
With many slits, the bright lines are thin and sharp, with wide dark gaps between them. This makes them easier to measure than the broad fringes from two slits.
For a given d, a longer wavelength gives a larger angle. So a grating spreads white light into colours and splits a light source into its separate wavelengths. Measuring θ lets us find λ.
draft.remember: More slits make sharper lines, and d sin θ = mλ links the angle to the wavelength.

a.q: Compared with a double slit of the same spacing, why is a diffraction grating better for measuring wavelengths?
opts: Its bright lines are thin and sharp, so angles are precise
Its bright lines are wider, so they are easier to see
It stops light of some wavelengths from passing through
It makes all wavelengths leave at the same angle
a.why: Light from many slits interferes to give thin, sharp bright lines, so the angle θ can be measured precisely. Wider lines would make the angle harder to read, not easier.
a.clue: Think about what many slits do to the width of each bright line.

b.q: A grating has slit spacing d. Red and blue light both pass through it. In the first order (m = 1), which statement is correct?
opts: Red light is bent to a larger angle than blue light
Blue light is bent to a larger angle than red light
Red and blue light leave at the same angle
Red light is not bent but blue light is
b.why: Since sin θ = mλ/d, a larger wavelength gives a larger angle for the same d and m. Red has a longer wavelength than blue, so it is bent more. The idea that shorter wavelengths bend more is a common mistake.
b.clue: Rearrange d sin θ = mλ to get sin θ on its own.

a.best: Its bright lines are thin and sharp, so angles are precise

b.best: Red light is bent to a larger angle than blue light
